basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/QCryptonPQCScannerAgent/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. Post-quantum cryptography readiness for internal networks and appliances. The QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent deploys inside your VNet and probes TLS posture on F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, Fortinet, and internal Azure endpoints. Ships with data connector, 6 analytic rules, workbook, and Teams-notification playbook. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 6, **Playbooks:** 1 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
Displays post-quantum cryptographic readiness posture for internal network appliances and endpoints scanned by the QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

A network appliance (F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, or Fortinet) is presenting a
TLS certificate signed with a classical algorithm (RSA/ECDSA) that is vulnerable to quantum attack.
These appliances terminate TLS for critical internal traffic and are prime harvest-now-decrypt-later
targets. Migrate to PQ-hybrid certificates or deploy QCrypton PQC Engine to front the appliance.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: Internal endpoint using TLS protocol below 1.3

options.text:
A VNet-internal Azure endpoint or network appliance is accepting TLS below version 1.3. Only
TLS 1.3 supports negotiation of hybrid post-quantum key exchange groups (X25519MLKEM768). Internal
endpoints on legacy TLS cannot be upgraded to PQ without a protocol change. Upgrade the minimum
TLS version to 1.3 to enable PQC readiness.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: New quantum-vulnerable appliance or internal resource appeared

options.text:
A network appliance or internal Azure endpoint with quantum-vulnerable posture appeared that
was not observed in the previous 24-hour scan cycle. This may indicate a new deployment, a
configuration change, or a newly discovered endpoint that should have been provisioned with
PQ-hybrid cryptography.

elements.name: analytic4
elements.label: PQC-ready appliance detected -- quantum-safe posture confirmed

options.text:
A network appliance has been confirmed as post-quantum ready. This may indicate a QCrypton PQC
Engine deployment on F5 BIG-IP, a hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) negotiation, or an
ML-DSA/ML-KEM certificate in use. This is a positive signal -- the appliance is protected against
harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

elements.name: analytic5
elements.label: High-risk internal endpoint with critical quantum vulnerability

options.text:
An internal endpoint or network appliance has a risk score above 20, indicating critical or high
severity quantum vulnerabilities. This may include expired certificates on appliances, RSA keys
shorter than 2048 bits, or multiple compounding vulnerabilities on the same endpoint. Immediate
remediation is recommended.

elements.name: analytic6
elements.label: Appliance certificate expiring within 30 days with classical algorithm

options.text:
A network appliance TLS certificate is expiring within the next 30 days and uses a classical
(quantum-vulnerable) signature algorithm. Certificate renewal is an ideal time to migrate to a
PQ-hybrid certificate. If the certificate is renewed with a classical algorithm, the
harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure window resets for the new validity period.

This solution installs the Playbook templates to help implement your Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) operations. After installing the solution, these will be deployed under Playbook Templates in the Automation blade in Microsoft Sentinel. They can be configured and managed from the Manage solution view in Content Hub.
